notes:
Summary: Sierra Lattice is evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for latency-sensitive chat + routing workloads. Primary ask is alignment on latency SLO definitions and measurement boundaries before procurement. They have strict compliance (SOC2, KMS) and want VPC-connect with optional on-prem staging.

Key latency goals (customer stated):
- Non-streaming (complete response): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 100ms, p99 < 220ms (90th percentile of production tokens currently)
- Streaming / chat (time-to-first-byte / TTFB): p50 < 20ms, p95 < 50ms, p99 < 120ms
- End-to-stream (full token emission) has separate SLO (depends on response length) — they want tail isolation for large payloads.

Measurement alignment issues to resolve:
- Client-side vs server-side timing: customer expects client SDK timestamps to be authoritative for SLOs. They want a hybrid approach: server-side traces for debugging, client-side as billing/SLA signal. Need to agree on which metrics are contractual.
- Streaming semantics: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) vs time-to-last-byte (TTLB). For streaming use-cases they prefer TTFB-based SLO for responsiveness and separate TTLB objectives for throughput/cost accounting.
- pXX definitions: agree on measuring latency at token emission vs request completion for batch vs streaming. Proposal: p50/p95 on request-complete for non-streaming; p50/p95 TTFB for streaming; p99 measured on server-side trimmed of known noisy infra (cold starts, failed envs) with explicit exclusion list.
- Instrumentation: recommend SDK-level UTC microsecond timestamps, request IDs propagated via header (x-rl-request-id), server spans annotated with model-variant, cache-hit, batch-size, kv-cache-hit-rate. Will deliver instrumentation checklist.
notes_followups: SLA negotiation points: define outage definitions, acceptable p99 windows, credits for sustained p99 breaches > 3 consecutive hours
Throughput guarantees: customer wants a committed baseline of 20k tokens/sec sustained across peak 8h window with 2:1 burst capacity for sudden spikes
Reserved GPU planning: suggestion 8 x A100-equivalent reserved nodes for initial commitment (based on their request mix), plan for autoscale + burst to shared pool
Batching & KV cache: heavy emphasis on warm KV cache for conversational context — measure p95 with cache-hit >= 85%. If cache warm-up drops expected performance, define pre-warm schedule in runbook
Synthetic load plan: two streams — (1) short-chat synthetic (avg len 32 tokens, 85% streaming), (2) long-report generation (avg len 512 tokens) to capture TTLB tails
Measurement buckets: define request classes (chat-short, chat-long, rerank-embed), maintain separate p50/p95/p99 per class
Client instrumentation ask: SDK to send tcp connect time, tls handshake, proxy hop durations — we will correlate with server spans to attribute latency
Fallback policy: customer wants automatic route to smaller model variants on overload but only if semantic degradation within defined delta — need to specify evals to quantify degradation
Security/contract asks: data residency clause for EU customers, KMS integration for keys stored via customer-managed keys, SOC2 report included in contract appendix
poC_plan: 2-week POC. Week 1: baseline capture + synthetic streaming load (3 days), week 1 end: config tweaks (batching/window), week 2: production replay with live traffic mirror (48h), on-site joint run for latency validation and server-side traces. Deliverables: instrumentation guide, perf report with p50/p95/p99 breakouts, recommended reserved GPU count and autoscale thresholds.

Will request standard enterprise clauses: uptime SLA, performance credits, and 30-day ramp for reserved capacity. Pricing team to produce draft by 2025-02-20.
